--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.layout_random()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Scatter the nodes uniformly at random over a square. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.layout_random()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Scatter the nodes uniformly at random over a square. title: >- [Graph.layout_random()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Scatter the nodes uniformly at random over a square. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Scatter the nodes uniformly at random over a square. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5894-L6006){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.layout_random( scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random layout](../assets/graphs/layout-random.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, a ring of eight nodes with two chords, drawn on a circle. On the right, layout_random(seed=71) drops each node at a uniformly random point in a square, ignoring the edges, so the ring is scrambled." width="100%"} Each coordinate is drawn independently and uniformly from `[center - scale, center + scale)`. Edges play no part. A random layout is a baseline to compare other layouts against, and a starting point for the iterative layouts via their `initial=` argument. Unlike NetworkX's `random_layout()`, which always uses the unit square `[0, 1)^2` shifted by `center`, the square here is `scale=`-sized and centered, like the other layouts. Positions are stored as `[x, y]` lists in the `attr_name=` node attribute; see `layout_circular()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Half the side of the square. Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Center of the square, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` always gives the same positions. If `None` (default), the positions differ on every call. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the positions in. If `None` (default), uses `"pos"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `scale=` is not a positive number or `center=` is not a pair of numbers. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~layout_spring`) : Place nodes with a force-directed spring model. [](`~rescale_layout`) : Center and scale stored positions. [](`~plot`) : Draw the graph using stored positions. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every coordinate falls within `scale=` of the center: ::: {#a858a163 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(100) pos = graph.layout_random(seed=3, return_dict=True) max(max(abs(x), abs(y)) for x, y in pos.values()) <= 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ### A floor plan, scrambled Random positions ignore the edges, so they show how much a layout does. The rooms of a two-story office, joined where a door leads from one to the other, placed at random on the left and on the plan on the right. Only the plan shows the halls and the rooms off them: ::: {#369ad3f7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} offices = ec.offices().layout_random(seed=3, attr_name="random") ``` ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#da85ed7d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} offices.plot( layout="random", label_by="label", width=360, height=360, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#fcbb5c6f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} offices.plot( layout="pos", label_by="label", width=360, height=360, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: The same `seed=` gives the same positions. A random layout is also a common starting point for the force-directed layouts, through their `initial=` argument. [Layouts](../user-guide/layouts.qmd#layouts-from-structure) explains why a random layout makes a useful baseline.
